sentences.text: : Judgment :
The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic Basavaraj.
N vs K.S.R.T.C

1 accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 02.04.2021 at about 5.45 am., when the petitioner was passenger in a NERTC bus bearing reg.No.KA-36-F-1614 and was proceeding from Rampura, Molakalmuru taluk to Bangalore and while proceeding so on Vatal Nagaraj road at RR junction, Okalipuram Bangalore, the driver fo the said bus driven the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner without noticing the road hump, jumped the road hump and as a result of which the petitioner lost the control and fell down from the seat SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.4401/2021 inside the bus and caused the accident.
Due to impact, the petitioner sustained injuries and immediately shifted to St.John's college Hospital and took conservative treatment.
Due to the injuries sustained in the said accident, he had incurred huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 41 years, working as Police Head Constable and posted to work at Rampura Molakalmuru taluk, Chitradurga district and drawing a salary of Rs.43,016/- per month.
The Malleshwaram Traffic Police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the NEKRTC bus bearing reg.No.KA-36-F-1614 in crime No.12/2021 punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC.
The respondent is the R C owner of the NEKRTC and the bus was driven by its employee at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay the SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.4401/2021 compensation.
3. After service of summons, the Respondent has appeared through its counsel and filed its objection to main petition.
Respondent filed its objection by denying the petition averments.

Respondent has denies the age,
occupation, income and injury sustained by the petitioner.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:
:: ISSUES::
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 02.04.2021 at about 05.45 am., when petitioner was passenger in a NEKRTC bus bearing reg.No.KA-36-F-1614 and was proceeding from Rampura, Molakalmuru taluk to Bangalore, while proceedings so on Vatal Nagaraj road, at RR junction, Okalipuram, Bangalore, at that the driver of the said bus driven the same at high speed in a reckless, rash and negligently, as a result of which SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.4401/2021 petitioner fell down and sustained Basavaraj.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149128008/
2
grievous injury, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,
from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
5. The petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 19 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.19.
He has examined his witnesses Dr. B.Vishwanath, as PW.2 and got marked two documents as Ex.P.20 and 21.

On the other hand, on behalf of the respondent driver of the KSRTC bus has examined as RW.1, its conductor has examined as RW.2 and Assistant Security Inspector, Raichur Division, NEKRTC has examined as RW.3 and got five documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5 and closed its side evidence.
6. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused materials on the entire records.

7. My findings to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.4401/2021  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 REASONS 8. Issue No.1: In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19.
He has re-iterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed for his examination-in-chief.
9. It is relevant to note that the respondent has denied the nature of accident.
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of NEKRTC bus.

10. Petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and in his evidence has stated that on on 02.04.2021 at about 5.45 am., when the petitioner was passenger in a NERTC bus bearing reg.No.KA-36-F-1614 and was proceeding from Rampura, Molakalmuru taluk to Bangalore and while proceeding so on Vatal Nagaraj road at RR junction, Okalipuram Bangalore, the driver for the said bus driven SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.4401/2021 the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner without noticing the road hump, jumped the road hump and as a result of which the petitioner lost the control and fell down from the seat inside the bus and caused the accident.
11. PW.1 in support of his version, he has produced the certified copy of FIR, complaint, rough sketch, spot panchanama, IMV report and charge sheet at Ex.P.1 to 5 and 7.

3 12.
I have perused Ex.P.1 to 5 and 7.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 02.04.2021 at about 5.45 am., and the FIR at Ex.P.1 in crime No.012/2021 came to be registered on 09.04.2021 at around 14.30, at Malleshwaram Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279,
337 of IPC.
and complaint at Ex.P.2 was lodged by petitioner on 09.04.2021, Ex.P.3 - rough sketch drawn on 09.04.2021 wherein it discloses that accident occurred at Vatal Nagaraj Road, Ex
. P.4 - spot panchanama discloses the nature of accident same SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.4401/2021 as in petition.

Further the records reveal that thereafter, the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet at Ex.P.7 against the rider of the offending motor cycle for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC and under Section 134( A&B), 187 of MV Act.
13. The learned counsel for the respondent has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1, PW.1 denied contention of the respondent.
The learned counsel for the respondent has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.4401/2021 one.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of the offending Bus which belongs to the respondent.
Therefore, respondent has failed to prove its contention as the petitioner sustained injuries due to the alleged accident by the offending bus.
However, the charge sheet is also not challenged by the respondent.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:
The Petitioner stated that due to the accident he has sustained L-1 anterior wedge compression fracture.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.6 - wound certificate, Ex.

P.9 - discharge summary,
Ex.P.10 - follow up records, Ex.P.11 - MRI scan, Ex.P.12 - medical bills of Rs.14,514/-, Ex
.P.13 - medical prescriptions and Ex.P.19 - X-rays.
15. As per Ex.P.6 - wound certificate, he has sustained L1 wedge compression fracture.

PW.1 has also examined Dr.B.Vishwanath as PW.2, he has deposed SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.4401/2021 that,
petitioner sustained anterior wedge compression of L1 Vertebrae and on examination he has found diffuse tenderness over lower back, scoliosis at L.S.Spine, X-ray of L.S.Spine: healed wedge compression fracture at L1 with loss of 25% height of L1 and he has advised L.S.belt application and physiotherapy L.S.Spine so as to avoid further deterioration.
Further he has deposed that, as per guidelines of Central Government of India gazette notification he suffers from 7% physical disability to the whole body.
During examination in chief he has produced OPD Card and X-ray marked at Ex.P.20 and 21.

4 16.
PW.1 further deposed that, he was working as Police Head Constable, Karnataka State Police Department, Chitradurga District and was drawing salary of Rs.43,016/- per month.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Along with this contention he has produced 3 pay slips marked at Ex.P.14 to 16, leave certificate marked at Ex.P.17 and Identity card marked at Ex.P.18.

Due to the injuries SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.4401/2021 sustained in the accident, he had not attended the duty for a period of two months and he lost his earned leave for one month and commuted leave for one month.
17. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in road traffic accident.
The PW.1 has produced 8 medical bills amounting to Rs.14,514/- to show the expenses incurred by him.

The respondent has produced the documents in Ex.R2 and Ex.R3, which discloses that the petitioner has spent the medical expenses of Rs.11,591/- and petitioner has not reimbursement from the government scheme in police department,
18.
Therefore it can come to the conclusion that, petitioner has not suffered any loss of income during the period of treatment and during the period of rest.

Hence, by considering the nature of injuries, evidence of doctor, age of the petitioner, treatment taken in the hospital and expenses insured for treatment as stated supra, SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.4401/2021 considering the pain and sufferings of the Petitioner, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.75,000/- as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
19. LIABILITY:-
As it is already held that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of NEKRTC bus, therefore respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Respondent shall deposit the compensation amount with interest @ 6% p.a. within three months from the date of this Order.
With the observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.3:

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following :-
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for  SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.4401/2021  compensation of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent being RC owner of NEKRTC Bus is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment upon proper verification Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw an award accordingly.
